cases.name: native alert work parks and coalesces under its runtime owner
cases.scenario: A desktop logs in with old unread receipts, then remains quiet, receives a burst and switches accounts while a native presentation is pending. Review the native alerts path. Identify the distinction between a source guarantee and actual OS measurements.
rubric: Initial observation uses the captured launch high-water. Old receipt backlog does not replay as live activity.
Quiet observation awaits a scoped change. The owner uses a one-shot delay only for pending work and bounds receipt reads to one batch of up to eight per second.
A change during the bounded read or presentation can remain pending. Runtime retirement and authority protect native presentation.
Native presentation is independent of durable renderer acknowledgement. Source or simulated-clock evidence does not establish OS wakeup, energy or CPU savings.

cases.name: device-link status wakes on scoped events and retains explicit repair
cases.scenario: Account A sees document and sync-state changes, including notifications from account B. A status read stalls beyond the UI watchdog, the dialog hides, and a new runtime replaces the old dialog. Review current-owner refresh, fallback and read ownership.
rubric: Device-link status responds to same-owner sync-status and compatible broad state invalidations. Other owners and pure document signals do not start the read.
The visible fallback remains five seconds to cover time-derived availability. Account-login status stays on its separate cadence and meaning.
A caller timeout does not release the actual native read slot or start overlapping work within the current reader. An admitted pending wake is bounded.
Hidden state parks the timer, activation restores an observation, and dialog retirement removes the listeners and suppresses stale publication.

cases.name: native notification permission uses timer-free foreground recovery
cases.scenario: A user returns from system notification settings. Focus and visibility fire in the same turn, a second observer is mounted, and the active observer stops while an activation is pending. Review periodic work, permission checks and authorization.
rubric: The owner checks once at startup and uses the shared recovery component without a periodic timer.
Foreground signals from the same turn coalesce. Permission reads share admitted native work and never request authorization themselves.
Disposal removes listeners and prevents a queued foreground callback from running after disposal.
Observation errors and unknown permission are handled without covering up the distinction between a browser or model check and a real OS prompt.

cases.name: AI guidance routes scheduling changes to owners and preserves recovery
cases.scenario: An AI contributor wants to replace a polling loop and add consumers for a retry, a foreground permission recheck and an expiry. Evaluate discoverability and registration policy. Distinguish existing components from proposed contracts.
rubric: Contributor instructions route scheduling and event changes to the maintained guides. The guides link real owners and separate shipped entry points from proposed shared interfaces.
Guidance distinguishes deadlines, retries, foreground recovery, active cadence and committed business events, including clock choice, overdue work and bounded concurrency.
Registration describes authority, lifecycle, disposal, in-flight cancellation and stale completion. Recovery protects against missed notifications and restarts.
Verification calls for idle, active, return-to-idle and relevant failure controls. Simulated-time or model results cannot be counted as native performance measurements.
